pairs.question: Sed et si credat aliquis, invito domino se rem commodatam sibi contrectare, domino autem volente id fiat, dicitur furtum non fieri. Cum Titius servum Maevii sollicitaverit, ut quasdam res domino subriperet et ad eum perferret, et servus id ad Maevium pertulerit, Maevius, dum vult Titium in ipso delicto deprehendere, permisit servo quasdam res ad eum perferre, utrum furti an servi corrupti iudicio teneatur Titius, an neutro?
pairs.answer: Nos huiusmodi calliditati obviam euntes, per nostram decisionem sanximus, non solum furti actionem, sed etiam servi corrupti contra eum dari.
pairs.derivation: Authorial-rhetorical question and its decision. The asking-frame 'unde illud quaesitum est' is dropped as meta-narration of the asking. The interrogative is one contiguous sentence ('cum Titius... permisit servo quasdam res ad eum perferre, utrum furti an servi corrupti iudicio teneatur Titius, an neutro?'); the preceding 'Sed et si credat aliquis... dicitur furtum non fieri' is kept verbatim as setup so the scenario is intelligible. The answer skips the non-answering preamble 'et cum nobis super hac dubitatione suggestum est et antiquorum prudentium super hoc altercationes perspeximus, quibusdam neque furti neque servi corrupti actionem praestantibus, quibusdam furti tantummodo' (deflection: reports prior opinions, does not decide) and starts at the operative ruling 'nos huiusmodi calliditati obviam euntes...'. It ends at the first full stop ('contra eum dari'); the dangling colon is dropped and what follows ('licet enim is servus deterior...') is justifying elaboration, not the answer.

pairs.question: Qui res alienas rapit, tenetur quidem etiam furti. Quis enim magis alienam rem invito domino contrectat quam qui vi rapit?
pairs.answer: Ideoque recte dictum est, eum improbum furem esse.
pairs.derivation: Authorial-rhetorical pair from the title opening (line 38). The question is the parenthetical interrogative 'quis enim magis alienam rem invito domino contrectat quam qui vi rapit?'; the preceding clause 'Qui res alienas rapit, tenetur quidem etiam furti' is kept verbatim as setup so 'eum' in the answer has a referent. The parentheses are presentational and dropped. The answer is the immediately following sentence 'ideoque recte dictum est, eum improbum furem esse', which resolves the rhetorical question (the violent robber is the worst sort of thief); it ends at the close of the parenthesis, before 'sed tamen propriam actionem eius delicti nomine praetor introduxit', which turns to a new point.
